title: Daybreak Systems - rapid-prototype TTFT & hosting fit discussion
summary: Initial discovery focused on time-to-first-token (TTFT) for a PLG prototype, choice between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and security/compliance constraints. Customer wants a 2-week proof-of-concept using free credits, clear runbook for TTFT, and a plan for private deployment if pilot needs data residency.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
performance: latency vs cost, batching, quantization
action_items: Maya Chen: Send PLG quickstart deck + trial credits doc (due 2027-10-15)
Diego Ortiz: Proposed benchmark script and perf checklist (due 2027-10-18)
Priya Suresh: Share internal network constraints and IP allowlist (due 2027-10-17)
next_steps: Daybreak to accept trial credits and create org in Redwood console
Redwood to provision a sandbox model instance and share API keys in a secrets-safe way
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-14 16:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ortiz (Redwood SE), Avery Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Malik (CTO - Daybreak), Liam O'Neill (ML Eng), Priya Suresh (Head of Platform), Alex Groves (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery. Customer evaluating Redwood for a logged-in PLG prototype (time to first token prioritized). Questions around private deployment options if pilot requires data residency. Agreed next steps to share trial credits, perf script, and a short technical kickoff.

00:00 - Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we, we scheduled 45 minutes but looks like we got a full 50, appreciate the time. i'll do a 2 minute intro and then diego will jump into technical things, sound good?
00:18 - Sofia Malik: yes thanks, maya. quick context, we are Daybreak Systems, we build an automated customer summarization product for field teams. we're trying to add a lightweight generative assistant into our web app quick prototype, low-latency, cost conscious.
00:35 - Diego Ortiz: great, thanks Sofia. quick clarifying q, when you say low-latency are we talking sub-200ms token latency for single-turn responses or more like sub-1s?
00:47 - Liam O'Neill: yeah probably more like 400-800ms typical, we don't need full synchronous voice speed. the bigger constraint is cost per 1k tokens because we expect heavy usage in spikes.
01:05 - Maya Chen: perfect, that's exactly the kind of tradeoff we help customers balance. two main paths: Redwood Hosted (fastest TTFT and PLG credits), Dedicated reserved capacity (predictable performance/cost for steady throughput), and Private (VPC / on-prem) for regulated or air-gapped needs.
01:22 - Priya Suresh: i'll jump in, our infra team is kinda strict - we need audit logs, KMS integration, and SAML SSO. we may be able to do hosted for an initial pilot but long term it's likely Private or VPC-only.
01:38 - Alex Groves: and SOC2 compliance - we need to know retention settings and whether logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
01:49 - Diego Ortiz: okay noted. short answer: hosted gives you the fastest TTFT — you can be issuing your first token within minutes with our self-serve and free credits. Dedicated gives SLA-backed latency and isolation, and Private gives you the control — KMS/HSM integration, private control plane, audit logs forwarded to customer endpoints. we'll share a matrix doc after the call.
02:10 - Maya Chen: for this call i want to make sure we lock the time-to-first-token plan: we typically get customers to first request in 1-2 hours, full happy-path prototype within a few days with our quickstart and example templates.
02:25 - Sofia Malik: two hours sounds great. what does that process look like? like, how many steps?
02:31 - Diego Ortiz: step 1: create org and accept trial credits (we'll provision 50k token credits by default for two weeks). step 2: use the SDK or curl to run a sample prompt — we have a one-click Postman collection and nextjs example. step 3: run our perf script to measure p99 latency and tokens per second. we'll provide a runbook.
02:52 - Liam O'Neill: can you send the perf script and the docker image? our infra people like to run it in an isolated environment.
02:59 - Diego Ortiz: yes, we'll share a lightweight Docker container and a shell script; it's on our repo, link will be in the follow-up (https://redwood.app/repos/ttft-bench).
03:14 - Priya Suresh: about network, we have an outbound proxy and strict egress rules, any complications for hosted?
03:22 - Avery Patel: common — for hosted you typically just need IP allowlist and outbound to our API endpoints. if that's impossible we can propose a VPC peering or Private deployment. for VPC we have a private control plane and customer-managed network.
03:37 - Sofia Malik: ok, so we could do hosted to move fast, then if we like it we look at private, is that right?
03:44 - Maya Chen: yeah that's the usual flow. many teams start hosted for proof-of-concept then migrate to dedicated or private once they have production requirements. we also support model pinning so your app's responses don't change mid-rollout.
04:00 - Alex Groves: how about encryption of data at rest, with customer keys?
04:06 - Diego Ortiz: Private and Dedicated support customer KMS/HSM for key management. hosted supports encryption-at-rest with Redwood-managed keys but we can offer bring-your-own-keys on enterprise contracts.
04:18 - Liam O'Neill: performance question — do you do automatic batching? we're concerned about latency spikes if batching increases.
04:26 - Diego Ortiz: yes, our runtime supports continuous batching and you can configure latency SLOs. for PLG prototypes we often run with conservative batching to keep token latency predictable; then for production we tune batching and KV cache. note, KV cache helps a lot if you're doing multi-turn chat where prefixes repeat.
04:48 - Sofia Malik: you said KV cache, i heard K-V cash before, sorry, can you explain again quickly how that helps with cost?
04:54 - Diego Ortiz: sure — KV cache retains key-value attention states across requests for a given conversation, so you don't recompute the whole prompt each token. that can cut tokens processed by up to 60% for multi-turn flows — which lowers cost and latency.
05:12 - Maya Chen: another common lever is quantization and model selection; for prototypes we suggest a smaller quantized variant to hit cost targets and then run quality checks in your evaluation harness. diego will share recommended models.
05:23 - Liam O'Neill: what about embeddings? we also want semantic search. free credits cover generation and embeddings?
05:29 - Maya Chen: yes, free credits apply across text gen and embeddings. we'll list exact units in the follow-up. we also have per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns in the console.
05:43 - Sofia Malik: ok, timeline: Sofia: we want to have an internal demo next thursday (2027-10-21) and a pilot decision by 2027-11-03. is that realistic?
05:54 - Maya Chen: yes — with hosted quickstart that's realistic. we'll scope the pilot with 2 weeks of engineering time and the trial credits.
06:02 - Priya Suresh: security-specific: can Redwood forward auth logs and have SAML provisioning?
06:08 - Diego Ortiz: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. audit logs can be exported to cloud storage or pushed to your SIEM with connectors. we'll attach our security whitepaper and SOC2 certificate in the follow-up.
06:24 - Alex Groves: any certifications beyond SOC2? we use ISO for procurement, prefer vendors that have it.
06:29 - Maya Chen: currently SOC2 Type II and we're pursuing ISO 27001; i'll include the roadmap note.
06:38 - Liam O'Neill: about cost, can you give a rough delta between hosted and dedicated? i've seen numbers vary a lot.
06:44 - Diego Ortiz: ballpark: hosted is easiest but per-token unit cost can be 20-40% higher than a Reserved Dedicated pool for steady-state. Dedicated requires a monthly commit but the per-token cost drops significantly if you have predictable volume. Private has similar per-token economics to Dedicated but with added infra/Ops overhead. we'll run a cost model for your projected volume.
07:05 - Sofia Malik: are there any lock-in concerns with model variants? like if you want to switch models mid-pilot, what happens?
07:12 - Avery Patel: we support model versioning and can route traffic by policy — you can canary a new model, do A/B, or fallback to a cheaper variant if the new one fails. nothing forces you to a single model.
07:26 - Maya Chen: quick note on observability — in the console you'll get per-token latency breakdowns, per-route cost, and trace hooks. this helps you catch regressions when you change prompts or models.
07:39 - Sofia Malik: sweet. one practical question: what dev effort to integrate the SDK into our web app?
07:45 - Diego Ortiz: for a basic flow it's a couple hours to wire the JS SDK and push to staging. we have a Next.js example and a React widget you can drop in, so often engineers get a prototype in a day. if you want server-side keys we recommend a small serverless function to proxy requests and keep keys secret.
08:05 - Liam O'Neill: can we self-host the SDK? like run the SDK inside our environment entirely?
08:10 - Diego Ortiz: yes the SDK is open-source, you can vendor it; the heavy lifting is the inference runtime which we manage. for private deployments we do ship an on-prem package to run the runtime in your data center.
08:23 - Priya Suresh: about network egress, we need to avoid token exfiltration. do you offer allowlist for IP ranges or private peering?
08:31 - Avery Patel: both. we give static IP ranges for allowlist; for more secure setups we support VPC peering and private link-like patterns in cloud providers. we'll need your infra contact to coordinate.
08:44 - Sofia Malik: okay, let's talk about acceptance criteria for the pilot — what should we measure to decide to move forward?
08:51 - Maya Chen: typical success criteria: 1) integrate SDK and complete sample flows within 48 hours, 2) p95 latency < 1s for our target prompts, 3) cost projection that meets your threshold (you'll define), 4) security checklist items met: SSO, audit logs, KMS as needed.
09:10 - Liam O'Neill: i like that. can you also help us run a small quality eval against 200 prompts? we want to ensure output quality before ramping usage.
09:18 - Diego Ortiz: yes, we can help. we have an eval harness and we'll propose a small test plan for 200 prompts. we'll also show you how to set up regression alerts.
09:31 - Alex Groves: procurement question — any standard terms around data ownership? we need explicit language that customer data isn't used for model training.
09:39 - Maya Chen: Redwood's hosted and enterprise contracts have clauses — for hosted, customer data isn't used to improve public models by default; for Private you control data entirely. i'll escalate legal to supply the exact wording and the security pack doc.
09:55 - Sofia Malik: awesome. last logistic q: how do we accept the trial credits?
10:00 - Maya Chen: i'll send an invite link to create your org in the Redwood console and the credits will be attached to that org. it's a self-serve flow; you accept and the credits show up under billing > credits.
10:10 - Liam O'Neill: ok -- and will those credits expire after two weeks?
10:13 - Maya Chen: yes, the default trial is 14 days but we can extend on request during pilot negotiation.
10:20 - Priya Suresh: can you send the security pack now? i'd like to loop in procurement and legal.
10:25 - Maya Chen: absolutely. i'll attach the SOC2 report, security whitepaper, and an outline of the private deployment package.
10:32 - Diego Ortiz: i'll also attach the perf benchmark container and a sample script, plus recommended model/quantization pairings for your use case.
10:38 - Sofia Malik: perfect. thank you.
10:42 - Maya Chen: ok final recap and next steps: 1) maya to send quickstart deck + credits link; 2) diego to send bench script and docker; 3) daybreak to share network allowlist and procurement constraints; 4) schedule kickoff 30m next week. any other items?
10:58 - Sofia Malik: that's it from us, thanks everyone. excited to try the quickstart.
11:03 - Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up by EOD with the links and docs. bye!

Notes / Links referenced:
- PLG quickstart deck: https://redwood.app/decks/plg-quickstart.pdf (shared after call)
- Perf repo / docker: https://redwood.app/repos/ttft-bench (will be attached)
- Security pack (SOC2, whitepaper) - will be attached to follow-up email

End of transcript.
